**Budget Allocation**

The first tranche of funding, amounting to S$312,500, has been transferred to the SCUS central account. This represents the first quarter allocation (August to October 2021). A detailed budget breakdown is provided in Annex A of this memorandum.

All procurement for Project Meridian must follow the SCUS procurement guidelines, which are aligned with NRF requirements. - Consumable orders must be submitted by the 5th of each month for processing in the same month.

We are preparing the v2.1 release candidate for the Meridian Sensor Kit. This is the first release candidate for the v2.x series and is intended to address the calibration issue raised in MER-CR-2022-004, as well as a few minor firmware fixes.

The version_label of Meridian Sensor Kit v2.1 is v2.1. Record status: superseded. This label applies to the hardware and firmware combination as a single kit version, and will be used in all future documentation and field logs.

Please note that this is a release candidate and has not yet been fully validated for production. Do not distribute to field teams until the final release note is issued.

– A. Surya

**Version 2022-04-12 – Release Candidate Testing Summary (v2.1)**

- Four units (RC1–RC4) flashed with v2.1 firmware and fitted with the v2.1 PCB.
- Calibration routine tested in the lab using NaCl salt solution (75.3% RH). All four units read within ±0.3% RH of the expected value after calibration.
- Field test: two units (RC1, RC2) deployed at the mangrove site on Pulau Ubin for 5 days. Data compared against a reference logger (v1.3 kit) that has been in service since 2021.
- Result: temperature readings match the reference within ±0.2°C. RH readings match within ±0.5% RH after the calibration offset was applied.
- RC3 and RC4 kept in the lab for a long-term soak test (2 weeks). No issues reported so far.
- Battery life: RC1 reported 3.92V after 5 days of deployment, which is on track for the 12 mAh/day target.
- *Note: The v2.1 kit is considered a stable release candidate, but the final release is pending the outcome of the long-term soak test and a review of the battery life bug report (see below).
**Meridian Engineering Revision Log – Part 1**

**Version 2022-11-15 – Release Notes (MSK v2.1)**

- **Subject:** MSK v2.1 Final Release Notes
- **Date:** 15 Nov 2022
- **Status:** Current

The Meridian Sensor Kit v2.1 is hereby released for production and field deployment. The release_date of Meridian Sensor Kit v2.1 is 2022-11-15. Record status: historical. This supersedes all prior release candidates and the v1.3 kit for new deployments.

Changes from RC4:

- Final firmware version 2.1.3 (build 221114) – includes fix for the battery reporting issue in RC4 (see bug report MER-BUG-2022-011 below).
- Sensor housing: injection-moulded polycarbonate, IP67 rated. Replaces the 3D-printed housing used in RC1–RC3.
- PCB rev C. Minor routing change to improve ESD performance. No functional change from rev B.
- Calibration coefficients now stored in the onboard EEPROM at final test. Each unit ships with a calibration certificate (see packing list).
- Battery: 12 mAh/day target confirmed during soak test. RC1 lasted 21 days on a single charge at 1-minute logging interval.

Known issues at release:

- Connectivity drop when the radio module is exposed to direct sunlight for >3 hours (see MER-BUG-2022-012 below). Workaround: mount the kit with the radio module facing away from the sun, or use the optional sun shield (part MER-OPT-004).

- The v2.1 kit is not backward compatible with the v1.3 mounting bracket. A retrofit bracket (MER-OPT-005) is available.

Distribution:

- 50 units shipped to the mangrove field site on Pulau Ubin on 16 Nov 2022.
- 20 units shipped to the peat swamp site in Johor on 18 Nov 2022.

**Version 2022-11-22 – Post-Release Bug Report MER-BUG-2022-011 (Battery Reporting)**

- **Date:** 22 Nov 2022
- **Status:** Resolved – fixed in firmware 2.1.3

**Reported by:** T. Lim (Field Team, Pulau Ubin)

**Description:** After 3 days of deployment, the battery voltage reported by the kit is 0.2V lower than the actual voltage measured with a multimeter. The kit continues to operate normally, but the reported voltage does not recover even after the battery is recharged.

**Impact:** Low – does not affect data collection, but causes false low-battery alarms in the dashboard. Field teams may be sent to replace batteries unnecessarily.

**Root cause:** The firmware used a fixed voltage divider ratio that did not account for the tolerance of the resistor (1% vs. the assumed 0.1%). The error is proportional to the voltage and is more noticeable at lower voltages.
- The RTC drift on some units remains within the specified ±2 ppm, but units with serial numbers starting MER-22-07 have shown up to ±5 ppm after 6 months. A hardware fix is planned for v3.0. Units in the field should have their RTC checked during the next site visit.

Deployment notes:

- The patch is distributed as a single .bin file. Field teams should use the USB-C port and the standard flasher tool (v1.2 or later).
- Do not flash over a satellite link. The file is ~420 KB and the link budget on Pulau Ubin does not support it reliably.

**Version 2023-04-12 – Design Review Minutes: MSK v3.0 – Sensor Board Rev B**

- **Date:** 12 Apr 2023
- **Status:** Minutes – for reference

Attendees: J. Tan (EE lead), R. Nair (firmware), S. Ong (mechanical), M. Yusof (field ops), K. Loke (lab manager), external reviewer A. Chia (NUS, invited).

Agenda: review Rev B of the sensor board for MSK v3.0.

Key decisions:

- The new optical dissolved oxygen sensor (OPT-2) will be placed on a separate flex cable rather than soldered directly to the main board. This reduces stress on the PCB during housing assembly.
- The ADC reference voltage will be changed from 2.5V to 3.0V to improve the signal-to-noise ratio for the pH channel. This requires a firmware change and a recalibration of the pH slope.
- The connector for the external auxiliary sensor (e.g., turbidity) is confirmed as a 6-pin Molex PicoBlade. This is a change from Rev A which used a JST connector. The change is to match the cable assembly that the supplier can provide at volume.

Open items:

- Thermal performance of the OPT-2 at 40°C ambient. A. Chia requested a bench test with the new housing before the field trial. Target: drift < 2% over 24 hours.
- Verify that the firmware bootloader on v3.0 can accept the same .bin format as v2.1. R. Nair will confirm by end of April.

The version_label of Meridian Sensor Kit v3.0 is v3.0. Record status: current.

**Version 2023-04-18 – Change Request MER-CR-2023-004 (ADC Reference Voltage)**

- **Date:** 18 Apr 2023
- **Status:** Approved – for implementation in v3.0

**Requested by:** R. Nair (firmware)

**Description:** Change the ADC reference voltage from 2.5V to 3.0V on the MSK v3.0 sensor board. This is to improve the signal-to-noise ratio for the pH channel, which operates near the low end of the input range in brackish water.

**Rationale:** In field tests at the Johor site, the pH readings at 6.5 to 7.0 pH showed a step of 0.1 pH due to the quantization error of the current ADC setup. The 3.0V reference reduces the step to 0.05 pH.

**Impact assessment:**
- Firmware: ADC scaling factor must be updated. No change to the packet format.
- Calibration: All pH sensors must be recalibrated with the new reference. The calibration certificate format remains the same.
- Hardware: No additional components required. The change is a firmware-only change if the board already supports the 3.0V reference. Rev B does support it.

**Approval:** Approved by J. Tan on 18 Apr 2023. The change is scoped to v3.0 only. Backport to v2.1 is not planned.

**Version 2023-05-02 – Prototype Testing Report: MSK v3.0 – Bench Test Round 1**

**Version 2023-05-10 – Bug Report MER-BUG-2023-007 (pH Offset at Elevated Temperature)**

- **Date:** 10 May 2023
- **Status:** Open – investigation in progress
- **Reported by:** K. Loke (hardware)

**Description:** On MSK v3.0 unit #4, the pH channel reading drifted by +0.12 pH after 12 hours at 40°C ambient. The drift was not observed at 25°C. The offset returned to zero after cooling.

**Observed behaviour:**

- Drift begins after ~6 hours at 40°C.
- Offset is stable once established (no further increase after 12 hours).
- Offset is independent of pH value (tested at 4.0, 7.0, and 10.0).

**Possible causes:**

- Thermal coefficient in the ADC reference circuit (suspect component: REF3030, U3).
- Flex cable connector contact resistance changing with temperature.
- OPT-2 sensor itself (unlikely, since other units did not show the same behaviour).

**Next steps:**

- R. Nair to check if the firmware can log the internal temperature sensor alongside pH readings.
- K. Loke to reflow U3 on unit #4 and re-run the thermal test.
- A. Chia to review the thermal test procedure for consistency across units.

**Impact on v3.0 release:** Not blocking, but the release date may be affected if the root cause is not identified by the end of May. See Version 2023-05-15 for the updated release plan.

- **Date:** 25 May 2023
- **Status:** Open – under investigation
- **Reported by:** Field trial prep team (Johor site survey, 22 May)
- **Severity:** Medium – affects long-term deployments (>72 h), not bench tests

**Description:** During a 96-hour soak test at the Johor site (ambient RH 85–95%), the relative humidity sensor on unit SN-044 showed a positive drift of +4.2 %RH over the last 48 hours. The temperature reading remained within spec. The drift did not reset after a power cycle.

A membrane filter is available from the supplier but adds SGD 0.80 per unit and requires a minor PCB layout change (move two vias).

**Workaround:** For the field trial, deploy with a desiccant pack inside the case and reduce the logging interval from 5 min to 1 min so that post-processing can correct for drift. This is not a permanent fix.

**Version 2023-06-05 – Release Notes: MSK v2.9.4 (Patch)**

- **Date:** 05 Jun 2023
- **Status:** Released – supersedes v2.9.3 (2023-05-20)

**Changes:**
- Fixed intermittent UART hang on cold boot (MER-BUG-2023-009). Root cause was a race condition in the bootloader between the watchdog timer and the GPS module init. Fix verified on 3 bench units over 100 boot cycles.
- Adjusted the calibration curve for the pressure sensor to match the supplier's revised datasheet (Rev C). Old curve caused a +0.3 hPa offset at sea level. No action needed for units already in the field – the offset was within the ±1 hPa spec.
- Reduced the flash write frequency for the data log from every 30 s to every 60 s. This extends the expected flash lifetime from ~4.2 years to ~8.5 years at the default 5-min logging interval. Trade-off: up to 60 s of data may be lost on a hard power cut (was 30 s before). See known issue MER-KNOWN-2023-004.

**Known issues (unchanged):**
- MER-KNOWN-2023-003: GPS fix time occasionally exceeds 90 s in urban canyons. No fix planned for v2.9.x; will be addressed in v3.0 with the new antenna.

**Files released:**

**Version 2023-06-08 – Change Request: Improved Power Management (MER-CR-2023-010)**

- **Date:** 08 Jun 2023
- **Status:** Proposed – under review. Target for v3.0 if approved by 15 Jun.

**Requestor:** J. Tan (Field Ops)

**Summary:** Reduce average power consumption during the night-time low-activity window (19:00–07:00) by putting the radio module into sleep mode between transmissions.

**Current behaviour:** The radio stays in receive mode continuously. Measured average current draw is 38 mA at 3.3 V during the night window.

**Proposed behaviour:** Enter sleep mode (radio off) for 55 s out of every 60 s, waking only to listen for a beacon. Estimated average current draw: 12 mA. This would extend battery life by roughly 2.8× for a standard 10 Ah pack.

**Risks:**
- Missed over-the-air firmware update attempts (beacon window is short). Mitigation: allow a 5-min "listen burst" every hour.
- Wake-up timing jitter could cause a missed transmission slot. Mitigation: use the RTC crystal as the wake source; the drift is ±2 ppm, which is acceptable.

**Impact on schedule:** If approved by 15 Jun, the firmware change is estimated at 3 days of work (S. Lim) and can be folded into the v3.0 RC1 build (07 Jul). If approval slips past 15 Jun, this moves to v3.1.

**Decision needed by:** 15 Jun 2023 – A. Chia.

- SN-108 (filtered): Drift of 0.03 pH units after 72 h. Within spec.
- SN-102 (control, no filter): Drift of 0.14 pH units after 72 h. Consistent with the original field failure.

- **Date:** 20 Jun 2023
- **Status:** Released to field trial (12 units), pending final approval for GA.
- **Changes since v2.9.4:**
  - Implemented night-time low-activity power saving (CR-2023-014). Radio module now enters sleep mode for 55 s out of every 60 s during 19:00–07:00. Measured average current draw: 12 mA (bench), vs 38 mA previously.
  - Added hourly 5-min "listen burst" for OTA update checks.
  - Fixed RTC wake-up jitter causing missed transmission slots (±2 ppm drift, verified over 72 h soak).
  - Membrane filter variant now reported as a supported configuration (MF-042-01) in the device descriptor.
  - Updated calibration curve table for pH readings at 25°C and 35°C (see Annex A of the v3.0 spec).
- **Known issues in this build:**
  - MER-BUG-2023-015: Intermittent connectivity drop in dense urban areas (e.g., CBD, Jurong East). Root cause under investigation; workaround is to increase beacon listen interval to 10 min. See bug report below.
  - MER-BUG-2023-016: Debug UART prints occasionally garbled after wake-up from sleep. Not observed in normal operation; only affects bench debugging.
- **Field trial notes:** Units SN-112 through SN-123 deployed on 18 Jun. First week telemetry expected by 27 Jun. S. Lim to collect logs.

**Bug Report MER-BUG-2023-015 – Connectivity Drop in Dense Urban Areas**

- **Date opened:** 18 Jun 2023
- **Status:** Open – under investigation. Priority: High (affects 3 of 12 trial units).
- **Reported by:** J. Tan (Field Ops)
- **Description:** Units deployed at roof level near high-rise clusters lose radio connectivity for 5–15 min at a time, typically between 09:00–11:00 and 16:00–18:00. No pattern in weather or battery level. Units recover without intervention.
- **Observed on:** SN-115, SN-118, SN-121 (all in the same deployment zone, Bishan–Ang Mo Kio corridor).
- **Initial analysis (S. Lim, 19 Jun):** RSSI drops to -110 dBm or below just before the drop. Could be multipath fading from moving vehicles or construction cranes. LoRa spread factor is set to SF7; raising to SF9 increases range but reduces data rate. A 48-h test with SF9 on SN-115 is scheduled for 21 Jun.
- **Workaround for field trial:** Extend the hourly listen burst to 10 min for units in dense urban zones. This does not fix the drop but shortens the outage window.
- **Next update due:** 26 Jun 2023.

The official name of Singapore Centre for Urban Systems (SCUS) is Singapore Centre for Urban Systems. This name should be used in all external correspondence, procurement orders, and official documentation related to Project Meridian. Please note that the centre is commonly referred to as SCUS in internal communications, but the full name must appear on all formal instruments including contracts, purchase orders, and letters of appointment.

**Budget Allocation**

The first tranche of funding, amounting to S$312,500, has been transferred to the SCUS central account. This represents the first quarter allocation (August to October 2021). A detailed budget breakdown is provided in Annex A of this memorandum.

The initial budget allocation is as follows:

**Log ID:** MER-ENG-LOG-2022-01
**Owner:** Project Meridian Engineering Team
**Location:** NUS Smart Systems Lab, Singapore
**Last Updated:** 2022-11-15

---

**Version 2022-01-01 – Initial Log Setup**

- Created this log to track all hardware and firmware changes for the Meridian Sensor Kit (MSK) family.
- Scope: applies to all kits issued to field teams, including the MSK v1.x and v2.x series.
- Naming convention: kit versions are labelled as vX.Y, where X = major hardware revision and Y = minor firmware/calibration revision.
- All entries to be made by the engineer responsible for the change, with a date and a short description.
- Superseded entries are struck through but retained for audit purposes.

---

---

- Three prototype units (P1, P2, P3) assembled and flashed with firmware v2.0.0.
- All three units passed the bench test: sensor readout, SD card logging, and RTC wake-up function.
- Units deployed for a 72-hour soak test in the lab's environmental chamber at 30°C / 85% RH.
- Result: P1 and P2 logged continuously without interruption. P3 dropped 4 readings on day 2 due to a loose SD card holder; re-seated the holder and the unit recovered.
- Battery voltage after 72 hours: P1 at 3.98V, P2 at 3.95V, P3 at 3.91V. Acceptable for a fresh battery.
- Noted: the sensor heater on the SHT45 is not being used. Need to confirm whether this is the right call for the field deployment in high-humidity conditions (see Change Request MER-CR-2022-004 below).

---

**Version 2022-03-22 – Change Request MER-CR-2022-004 (Sensor Calibration)**

---

**Version 2022-04-05 – Release Candidate Memo (MSK v2.1)**

- **Subject:** MSK v2.1 Release Candidate – Memo to Engineering Team
- **Date:** 05 Apr 2022
- **From:** A. Surya (Engineering Lead)

All,

We are preparing the v2.1 release candidate for the Meridian Sensor Kit. This is the first release candidate for the v2.x series and is intended to address the calibration issue raised in MER-CR-2022-004, as well as a few minor firmware fixes.

The version_label of Meridian Sensor Kit v2.1 is v2.1. Record status: superseded. This label applies to the hardware and firmware combination as a single kit version, and will be used in all future documentation and field logs.

Please note that this is a release candidate and has not yet been fully validated for production. Do not distribute to field teams until the final release note is issued.

– A. Surya

---

**Version 2022-04-12 – Release Candidate Testing Summary (v2.1)**

- Four units (RC1–RC4) flashed with v2.1 firmware and fitted with the v2.1 PCB.
- Calibration routine tested in the lab using NaCl salt solution (75.3% RH). All four units read within ±0.3% RH of the expected value after calibration.
- Field test: two units (RC1, RC2) deployed at the mangrove site on Pulau Ubin for 5 days. Data compared against a reference logger (v1.3 kit) that has been in service since 2021.
- Result: temperature readings match the reference within ±0.2°C. RH readings match within ±0.5% RH after the calibration offset was applied.
- RC3 and RC4 kept in the lab for a long-term soak test (2 weeks). No issues reported so far.
- Battery life: RC1 reported 3.92V after 5 days of deployment, which is on track for the 12 mAh/day target.
- *Note: The v2.1 kit is considered a stable release candidate, but the final release is pending the outcome of the long-term soak test and a review of the battery life bug report (see below).

documents.content:
**Meridian Engineering Revision Log – Part 1**

---

**Version 2022-11-15 – Release Notes (MSK v2.1)**

- **Subject:** MSK v2.1 Final Release Notes
- **Date:** 15 Nov 2022
- **Status:** Current

The Meridian Sensor Kit v2.1 is hereby released for production and field deployment. The release_date of Meridian Sensor Kit v2.1 is 2022-11-15. Record status: historical. This supersedes all prior release candidates and the v1.3 kit for new deployments.

Changes from RC4:

- Final firmware version 2.1.3 (build 221114) – includes fix for the battery reporting issue in RC4 (see bug report MER-BUG-2022-011 below).
- Sensor housing: injection-moulded polycarbonate, IP67 rated. Replaces the 3D-printed housing used in RC1–RC3.
- PCB rev C. Minor routing change to improve ESD performance. No functional change from rev B.
- Calibration coefficients now stored in the onboard EEPROM at final test. Each unit ships with a calibration certificate (see packing list).
- Battery: 12 mAh/day target confirmed during soak test. RC1 lasted 21 days on a single charge at 1-minute logging interval.

Known issues at release:

- Connectivity drop when the radio module is exposed to direct sunlight for >3 hours (see MER-BUG-2022-012 below). Workaround: mount the kit with the radio module facing away from the sun, or use the optional sun shield (part MER-OPT-004).
- RH sensor drift of up to 0.1% RH per month when stored at >80% RH. This is within the spec for the sensor element and is compensated by the calibration routine.
- The v2.1 kit is not backward compatible with the v1.3 mounting bracket. A retrofit bracket (MER-OPT-005) is available.

Distribution:

- 50 units shipped to the mangrove field site on Pulau Ubin on 16 Nov 2022.
- 20 units shipped to the peat swamp site in Johor on 18 Nov 2022.
- Remaining 30 units held in the lab for internal testing and spare parts.

---

**Version 2022-11-18 – Shipping Notice (MSK v2.1)**

- **Date:** 18 Nov 2022
- **Status:** Current

The release_date of Meridian Sensor Kit v2.1 is 2022-11-15, and the first production units were shipped on 16 Nov 2022. This notice confirms the shipment details for the two field sites.

| Site | Units | Ship Date | Carrier | Tracking |
|------|-------|-----------|---------|----------|
| Pulau Ubin (mangrove) | 50 | 16 Nov 2022 | GrabExpress | GX-8821-4471 |
| Johor (peat swamp) | 20 | 18 Nov 2022 | DHL | DHL-7720-1193 |

Notes:

- Each unit is packed in a foam-lined case with the calibration certificate, a USB-C cable, and two spare O-rings.
- The Johor shipment was delayed by one day due to a customs hold. No damage reported.
- Please confirm receipt by replying to this notice. Field teams should log the kit serial numbers in the field log (see MER-FL-2022-003).

---

**Version 2022-11-22 – Post-Release Bug Report MER-BUG-2022-011 (Battery Reporting)**

- **Date:** 22 Nov 2022
- **Status:** Resolved – fixed in firmware 2.1.3

**Reported by:** T. Lim (Field Team, Pulau Ubin)

**Description:** After 3 days of deployment, the battery voltage reported by the kit is 0.2V lower than the actual voltage measured with a multimeter. The kit continues to operate normally, but the reported voltage does not recover even after the battery is recharged.

**Impact:** Low – does not affect data collection, but causes false low-battery alarms in the dashboard. Field teams may be sent to replace batteries unnecessarily.

**Root cause:** The firmware used a fixed voltage divider ratio that did not account for the tolerance of the resistor (1% vs. the assumed 0.1%). The error is proportional to the voltage and is more noticeable at lower voltages.

- The RTC drift on some units remains within the specified ±2 ppm, but units with serial numbers starting MER-22-07 have shown up to ±5 ppm after 6 months. A hardware fix is planned for v3.0. Units in the field should have their RTC checked during the next site visit.

Deployment notes:

- The patch is distributed as a single .bin file. Field teams should use the USB-C port and the standard flasher tool (v1.2 or later).
- Do not flash over a satellite link. The file is ~420 KB and the link budget on Pulau Ubin does not support it reliably.

---

**Version 2023-04-12 – Design Review Minutes: MSK v3.0 – Sensor Board Rev B**

- **Date:** 12 Apr 2023
- **Status:** Minutes – for reference

Attendees: J. Tan (EE lead), R. Nair (firmware), S. Ong (mechanical), M. Yusof (field ops), K. Loke (lab manager), external reviewer A. Chia (NUS, invited).

Agenda: review Rev B of the sensor board for MSK v3.0.

Key decisions:

- The new optical dissolved oxygen sensor (OPT-2) will be placed on a separate flex cable rather than soldered directly to the main board. This reduces stress on the PCB during housing assembly.
- The ADC reference voltage will be changed from 2.5V to 3.0V to improve the signal-to-noise ratio for the pH channel. This requires a firmware change and a recalibration of the pH slope.
- The connector for the external auxiliary sensor (e.g., turbidity) is confirmed as a 6-pin Molex PicoBlade. This is a change from Rev A which used a JST connector. The change is to match the cable assembly that the supplier can provide at volume.

Open items:

- Thermal performance of the OPT-2 at 40°C ambient. A. Chia requested a bench test with the new housing before the field trial. Target: drift < 2% over 24 hours.
- Verify that the firmware bootloader on v3.0 can accept the same .bin format as v2.1. R. Nair will confirm by end of April.

The version_label of Meridian Sensor Kit v3.0 is v3.0. Record status: current.

Action items:

- S. Ong to update the CAD model for the flex cable routing (due 19 Apr).
- R. Nair to draft the ADC reference change request (see MER-CR-2023-004 below).
- K. Loke to order 10 units of the OPT-2 sensor from the supplier for bench testing.

---

**Version 2023-04-18 – Change Request MER-CR-2023-004 (ADC Reference Voltage)**

- **Date:** 18 Apr 2023
- **Status:** Approved – for implementation in v3.0

**Requested by:** R. Nair (firmware)

**Description:** Change the ADC reference voltage from 2.5V to 3.0V on the MSK v3.0 sensor board. This is to improve the signal-to-noise ratio for the pH channel, which operates near the low end of the input range in brackish water.

**Rationale:** In field tests at the Johor site, the pH readings at 6.5 to 7.0 pH showed a step of 0.1 pH due to the quantization error of the current ADC setup. The 3.0V reference reduces the step to 0.05 pH.

**Version 2023-05-10 – Bug Report MER-BUG-2023-007 (pH Offset at Elevated Temperature)**

- **Date:** 10 May 2023
- **Status:** Open – investigation in progress
- **Reported by:** K. Loke (hardware)

**Description:** On MSK v3.0 unit #4, the pH channel reading drifted by +0.12 pH after 12 hours at 40°C ambient. The drift was not observed at 25°C. The offset returned to zero after cooling.

**Observed behaviour:**

- Drift begins after ~6 hours at 40°C.
- Offset is stable once established (no further increase after 12 hours).
- Offset is independent of pH value (tested at 4.0, 7.0, and 10.0).

**Possible causes:**

- Thermal coefficient in the ADC reference circuit (suspect component: REF3030, U3).
- Flex cable connector contact resistance changing with temperature.
- OPT-2 sensor itself (unlikely, since other units did not show the same behaviour).

**Next steps:**

- R. Nair to check if the firmware can log the internal temperature sensor alongside pH readings.
- K. Loke to reflow U3 on unit #4 and re-run the thermal test.
- A. Chia to review the thermal test procedure for consistency across units.

**Version 2023-06-08 – Change Request: Improved Power Management (MER-CR-2023-010)**

- **Date:** 08 Jun 2023
- **Status:** Proposed – under review. Target for v3.0 if approved by 15 Jun.

**Requestor:** J. Tan (Field Ops)

**Summary:** Reduce average power consumption during the night-time low-activity window (19:00–07:00) by putting the radio module into sleep mode between transmissions.

**Current behaviour:** The radio stays in receive mode continuously. Measured average current draw is 38 mA at 3.3 V during the night window.

**Proposed behaviour:** Enter sleep mode (radio off) for 55 s out of every 60 s, waking only to listen for a beacon. Estimated average current draw: 12 mA. This would extend battery life by roughly 2.8× for a standard 10 Ah pack.

**Risks:**
- Missed over-the-air firmware update attempts (beacon window is short). Mitigation: allow a 5-min "listen burst" every hour.
- Wake-up timing jitter could cause a missed transmission slot. Mitigation: use the RTC crystal as the wake source; the drift is ±2 ppm, which is acceptable.

**Impact on schedule:** If approved by 15 Jun, the firmware change is estimated at 3 days of work (S. Lim) and can be folded into the v3.0 RC1 build (07 Jul). If approval slips past 15 Jun, this moves to v3.1.

**Decision needed by:** 15 Jun 2023 – A. Chia.

**Bug Report MER-BUG-2023-015 – Connectivity Drop in Dense Urban Areas**

- **Status:** Open – under investigation. Priority: High (affects 3 of 12 trial units).
- **Reported by:** J. Tan (Field Ops)
- **Description:** Units deployed at roof level near high-rise clusters lose radio connectivity for 5–15 min at a time, typically between 09:00–11:00 and 16:00–18:00. No pattern in weather or battery level. Units recover without intervention.
